question: Is X-linked chondrodysplasia punctata 1 inherited ?
references: This condition is inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern. The gene associated with this condition is located on the X chromosome, which is one of the two sex chromosomes. In males (who have only one X chromosome), one altered copy of the ARSE gene in each cell is sufficient to cause the condition. In females (who have two X chromosomes), a mutation would have to occur in both copies of the gene to cause the disorder. Because it is unlikely that females will have two altered copies of this gene, males are affected by X-linked recessive disorders much more frequently than females. A characteristic of X-linked inheritance is that fathers cannot pass X-linked traits to their sons.

X-linked chondrodysplasia punctata 1 (CDPX1) is a rare genetic disorder. It is inherited in an X-linked dominant pattern. This means that the mutated gene responsible for the condition is located on the X chromosome. 

In females, who have two X chromosomes, a mutation in one of the X chromosomes is enough to cause the condition. Females with CDPX1 are usually more severely affected than males, who have only one X chromosome. If a male inherits the mutated gene, he is likely to be more severely affected and may not survive infancy.

CDPX1 is caused by mutations in the EBP gene, which is responsible for the production of a protein involved in the synthesis of plasmalogen, a type of phospholipid found in cell membranes. The disorder is characterized by skeletal abnormalities, including short stature, short limbs, and punctate calcifications in the cartilage.
